Ahmad Faruqui is an energy economist known for his work on electricity pricing, demand response, and the economics of energy. He has participated in research and consulting projects around the world, advising utilities, regulatory commissions, and government agencies on energy policy and tariff design.

Faruqui is particularly noted for his efforts in advancing the understanding and implementation of dynamic pricing models, such as time-of-use rates and critical peak pricing. These pricing models encourage consumers to adjust their energy consumption in response to price signals, leading to more efficient electricity use and grid stability.

He has published numerous articles, papers, and reports on topics related to energy economics, demand response, and pricing strategies. His work also often involves analyzing the impacts of advanced metering infrastructure and smart grids.

Faruqui has a strong academic background and has contributed to scholarly discourse through his involvement with various academic and professional associations in the energy sector. Beyond his published works, he is a frequent speaker at industry conferences and seminars, where he addresses both technical and policy issues in the energy sector.

If you are interested in specific details like his academic background, affiliations, or a list of his publications, I may suggest checking professional networking sites or academic databases for the most current and detailed information.
